trial_court: Family Court, Patna in Title Suit no. 11 of 2010
case_name: Vakil Prasad Singh vs Shail Kumari Singh & Ors

parties.respondent_defendant: Shail Kumari Singh and her two daughters Ritu Singh and Nitu Singh

facts_of_case: The respondent Shail Kumari Singh and her two daughters filed a suit for maintenance under Section 20(3) of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956. The claim was for marriage expense of their elder daughter Ritu Singh and reimbursement of marriage expenses of younger daughter Nitu Singh, totalling Rs. 20,00,000.

legal_principles.principle: A person who has sufficient means to pay for the marriage of his daughters is under an obligation to do so.
legal_principles.held: The defendant-appellant having married the plaintiff no. 1, Shail Kumari Singh and having been blessed with four daughters, then, abandoned her and the daughters to marry again, without any separation from the first wife.

legal_principles.principle: A person's property is not a secret and can be discovered through evidence.
legal_principles.held: The trial court, upon consideration of the evidence aforesaid, held that the defendant was under obligation to meet the marriage expenses of the daughters, and therefore, ordered and decreed the suit.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is being disposed of at this stage itself with the consent of parties.

use_for_drafting: appealing against order of lower court
